'''Leona Ruth Silver Aiken''' is an American President's Professor of psychology at [[Arizona State University]].

She is the co-author of two widely used [[statistics]] textbooks, ''Applied Multiple Regression/Correlation Analysis for the Behavior Sciences'' and ''Multiple Regression: Testing and interpreting interactions''.<ref>{{citation|url=https://isearch.asu.edu/profile/10618|title=Leona Aiken|publisher=[[Arizona State University]]|accessdate=2020-04-17}}</ref>

== Education and career==
Aiken graduated from [[Virginia Commonwealth University]] in 1965, and completed a PhD in psychology at [[Purdue University]] in 1970. She joined the [[Temple University]] faculty in 1969, and moved to Arizona State University in 1985. At Arizona State, she was given the President's Professorship in 2010.<ref name=cv/>

== Research ==
In terms of substantive research, Aiken specializes in women's health protective behavior. This research involves the application of a two-stage process, the first stage being psychosocial modeling, followed by the second stage of model based intervention.<ref name=cv>{{citation|url=https://isearch.asu.edu/profile/10618/cv/|title=Curriculum Vitae|publisher=Leona S. Aiken|accessdate=2020-04-17}}</ref> An example of this two-stage process can be seen in one of her studies, where peer perception of middle schoolers was used to model high school success, followed by suggestions on how peer perception should be reflected on by both the students and their parents.<ref>{{citation|url=https://asunow.asu.edu/20180921-new-asu-study-focuses-middle-school-kids%E2%80%99-peer-reputations-and-substance-use-and-academic|title=ASU study focuses on middle schoolers' reputations and their substance use and school achievement 6 years later |publisher=[[Arizona State University]]|accessdate=2020-04-17}}</ref>

In terms of methodological research, Leona Aiken specializes in models containing continuous variable interactions, which includes analysis of variance, [[Linear regression|multiple regression analysis]], [[multivariate analysis]], and structural equation modeling.

==Awards and honors==
Aiken is fellow of the [[Association for Psychological Science]],<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.psychologicalscience.org/fellows/fellows-new.cfm|title=APS Fellows|publisher=[[Association for Psychological Science]]|accessdate=2020-04-17|archive-date=2020-08-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813133237/https://www.psychologicalscience.org/fellows/fellows-new.cfm|url-status=dead}}</ref> of the [[American Psychological Association]] in 4 divisions,<ref>{{citation|url=http://fellows.apa.org/?_ga=2.65711406.1241899075.1587160263-46866220.1585932086|title=APA Fellows |publisher=[[American Psychological Association]]|accessdate=2020-04-17}}</ref> and of the [[Western Psychological Association]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://westernpsych.org/wpa-fellows/|title=WPS Fellows |publisher=[[Western Psychological Association]]|accessdate=2020-04-17}}</ref>
Leona Aiken is an elected member of the [[Society of Multivariate Experimental Psychology]],<ref>{{citation|url=https://smep.org/general-information/current-members|title=SMEP Current Members |publisher=[[Society of Multivariate Experimental Psychology]]|accessdate=2020-04-17}}</ref> and was president of the society in 2006.<ref>{{citation|url=https://smep.org/general-information/past-presidents|title=Past Presidents|publisher=[[Society of Multivariate Experimental Psychology]]|accessdate=2020-10-26}}</ref>
